items.snippet: Rounds of heavy rain in the U.S. Southwest flooded rivers and rapidly raised New Mexico’s second-largest reservoir.

items.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
items.snippet: Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight […]

items.title: SpaceX moves Starship Flight 15 booster to launch pad for 'squeeze test' ahead of epic double-catch attempt (photos)
items.snippet: SpaceX has moved its Starship Super Heavy booster to the pad to prep for the next test flight of the megarocket, a historic mission scheduled to launch this Friday (Nov. 13).

items.title: Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo reveal why they joined Andy Weir's sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' (interview)
items.snippet: We hooked up with Mackie, DeBose, and Lequizamo to learn more about this renaissance of audio dramas and what attracted them to board Weir's sci-fi thriller.

items.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
items.snippet: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. Here's why it mattered.

items.title: A distant exoplanet mysteriously vanished from sight. Astronomers just discovered why
items.snippet: Astronomers have solved the mystery of an exoplanet that "disappeared" after seven years of observations.

items.title: How to watch 'We Chose to Go to the Moon' online — stream space race stage show from anywhere
items.snippet: How to stream "We Chose to Go to the Moon", a live broadcast of the dazzling new stage retelling of the space race story.

items.title: SpaceX Starship Flight 15 live updates: Super Heavy rocket moved to launch pad for 1st Starship double landing test
items.snippet: Follow live updates as SpaceX attempts its Starship Flight 15 test flight with first double landings.

items.title: Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago
items.snippet: Scientists have uncovered fossils of a giant rodent that lived in Thailand 34 million years ago, revealing that enormous rodents evolved much earlier than previously thought. Named Yakamys sirindhornae, the ancient animal may have weighed around 66 pounds, roughly twice as much as other known rodents of its time.

items.title: Why heart attacks can still happen even when bad cholesterol is low
items.snippet: Even when bad cholesterol is brought down to healthy levels, some people remain at risk of heart attacks, and scientists may have discovered why. Researchers identified two types of fat-carrying particles that appear to promote inflammation and damage blood vessels through mechanisms beyond cholesterol buildup.

items.title: 237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian
items.snippet: A bizarre, heavily armored amphibian roamed the oceans 237 million years ago, despite the fact that modern amphibians cannot survive entirely in saltwater. Discovered in China, the giant salamander-sized creature may be the first known amphibian to have adapted to a fully marine existence.

items.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation
items.snippet: After more than a year of simulated life on Mars, four NASA volunteers have finally emerged from isolation, bringing a remarkable space exploration experiment to an end. Their experiences growing food, conserving resources, and overcoming Mars-like challenges could help NASA prepare for humanity's future on the Moon and Mars.

items.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
items.snippet: A breakthrough in telescope imaging could reveal countless alien worlds that have been hiding in plain sight. Scientists developed a new technique that uses a digital twin of the James Webb Space Telescope to remove the overwhelming glare of stars, making faint exoplanets two to 15 times easier to detect than with conventional methods. The technology has already uncovered a previously hidden plane

items.title: Scientists discover why some mosquitoes love you and others don't
items.snippet: A surprising new study reveals that mosquitoes have very different tastes in humans, with each species attracted to its own combination of skin odors, chemicals, and bacteria. The discovery challenges the idea of a universal mosquito magnet and could lead to more effective repellents against dangerous disease-spreading mosquitoes.

items.title: A mysterious 93-billion-mile cosmic structure may be the wreckage of colliding worlds
items.snippet: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has revealed surprising new details about a mysterious, 93-billion-mile-long cloud of dark, fluffy dust that may have formed when massive planetary bodies collided. The discovery challenges previous assumptions about the structure and offers new clues about the violent birth of planetary systems.

items.title: Comets may have destroyed life's ingredients instead of delivering them to Earth
items.snippet: A century-old theory about the origins of life on Earth may be wrong. New research from the University of Cambridge suggests that comets traveled too fast and struck at unfavorable angles for the fragile molecules needed for life to survive, making successful delivery extraordinarily unlikely. Surprisingly, Mars may have had a better chance of receiving these cosmic ingredients, although even ther

items.title: Paleontologists discover “one-in-a-million” fossil with 450-million-year-old soft tissue
items.snippet: Scientists have discovered a remarkably preserved 450-million-year-old fossil containing soft tissues from an ancient starfish relative, revealing unexpected details about marine life more than 200 million years before dinosaurs existed. Found in a museum collection, the extraordinarily rare specimen offers new clues about how Earth's earliest reef animals fed, survived, and evolved.

items.title: New study shows COVID value-added tax cut significantly boosted private consumption
items.snippet: In summer 2020, the German federal government lowered value-added tax from 19% to 16% for half a year as part of its COVID economic stimulus package. A new study, recently published in the journal Review of Economic Studies, uses survey data, data on retail purchases and an economic model to show the extent to which this measure influenced private consumption. The study found that lower-wealth hou

items.title: Coyotes are likely a permanent fixture on the Outer Banks of North Carolina
items.snippet: A new study reveals that coyote populations on the Outer Banks persist despite ongoing removal programs, posing a continued threat to shore-nesting birds and protected sea turtles. The study is the first in-depth assessment of coyote populations on barrier islands and has ramifications for understanding how coyotes may impact these and other barrier island ecosystems.

items.title: Simplified framework could make products' environmental impacts easier to assess
items.snippet: Life cycle assessment is used to quantify the environmental impact of products and services and forms an important basis for political decisions. However, the necessary data is always difficult to capture completely. A study by the Paul Scherrer Institute PSI now shows that four established hybrid methods can be reduced to just two: a first step towards open-source software that could enable such

items.title: Mental health app may help unemployed people find jobs, six-week trial suggests
items.snippet: Losing a job can be a life-shattering experience. And when depression complicates a job search, unemployment can become a vicious cycle. Now, a Northwestern University–led clinical trial suggests a new intervention may break that cycle: a phone app, named DRIVEN, that combines weekly self-guided mental health exercises (to reduce stress and increase motivation) with job-seeking strategies.

items.title: A new tool makes biodiversity conservation planning more efficient and reproducible
items.snippet: ZonationR is a new tool that simplifies the use of Zonation to identify priority areas for biodiversity conservation. It brings all stages of the conservation planning analysis together in one automated and reproducible workflow and helps users systematically explore and compare alternative conservation scenarios.

items.title: Genetic ancestry plays a key role in the migration of Cory's shearwaters
items.snippet: To what extent do genes influence the migratory routes of birds? The factors that determine the long-distance migrations of seabirds are not yet fully understood. Now, a study published in the journal Molecular Ecology reveals that, in the case of Cory's shearwater, an individual's genetic ancestry is a more significant factor in their migratory decisions than their social environment in the breed

items.title: Earliest known compact quasar pair poses a black hole growth puzzle
items.snippet: The oldest pair of compact quasars ever observed has been found only 900 million years after the Big Bang. Scientists say there is no theoretical explanation for how the pair of actively feeding black holes grew so massive at such an early time in the history of the universe. The pair of quasars has been given the Hawaiian nickname Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.

items.title: New organic iron-sulfur framework boosts photosynthesis and carbon fixation
items.snippet: Iron-sulfur clusters are ancient protein cofactors that are essential for electron transport, enzyme catalysis and photosynthesis. However, their sensitivity to oxygen and inherent instability have long hindered their practical application.

items.title: How ripples in space-time can reveal new exoplanets
items.snippet: The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets—worlds beyond our solar system—throughout our galaxy.

items.title: European eels transmit a herpesvirus through bites, revealing another route for fish infections
items.snippet: Contrary to what was previously believed, viruses infecting fish are not transmitted exclusively through water acting as an abiotic vector. A team of researchers from the University of Liège has demonstrated that a virus affecting European eels can spread very efficiently through biting during aggressive interactions between individuals.

items.title: The Handwritten Final Draft of Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' Speech Was Considered Lost. It Turned Out to Be Sitting in a Desk Drawer for Decades
items.snippet: Across seven yellow notepad pages, King is seen wrestling with word choice and revising his remarks the night before the March on Washington. The manuscript will head to auction in January and is expected to pull in more than $10 million

items.title: Octopuses Are the Ultimate Escape Artists. Now Scientists Know How the Creatures Contort Themselves to Squeeze Through Tiny Holes
items.snippet: A new study reveals the step-by-step process some octopuses use to cram themselves into tight openings. The findings could inspire new designs for soft robots used during search-and-rescue missions

items.title: What happens to mathematics when AI becomes an oracle?
items.snippet: Mathematician Steven Strogatz discusses his new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World .

items.title: Correcting quantum computer errors may be more complicated than expected
items.snippet: Correcting quantum computer errors is key for making the devices practical, but some types of errors, and the complications they could introduce, may be more likely to occur than we had thought

items.title: India’s efforts to clean its air need not slow its economic growth
items.snippet: The best interventions must address air pollution while supporting development priorities. Cleaner industrial processes may reduce emissions while improving efficiency. Clean cooking can reduce household smoke while improving convenience and health. Better waste management can reduce open burning while improving urban services

items.title: Physical pain often peaks during your working years, not in old age
items.snippet: A large new study has also found that people’s pain levels varied according to their income, geography, conditions like obesity, and habits like smoking
